hero.purpose: The single headline value overlaid on the usage chart. 26px, weight 650, tabular. Exactly one per view.

value.purpose: Readout-cell and trend values — the numbers in the grid. 15px, weight 600, tabular.

row.purpose: Entity names and their primary values in list rows. 11.5px.

body.purpose: Running sentences — the insight line, empty-state copy, disclosures. 10.5px.

meta.purpose: The working size of the instrument: labels, toggles, the sync pill, the view switcher, chips. 10px.

micro.purpose: The 8px floor. Rate-limit window labels and chart axis ticks only — never text a user must read to act.

mono.purpose: Geist Mono for raw model ids, session ids, and paths only — never decorative.

shadows.name: listbox
shadows.purpose: The view switcher menu and tooltips — the only everyday layer that leaves the plane.

shadows.name: modal
shadows.purpose: Confirmation dialogs in the management windows; the rare full-attention layer.

motion.name: control
motion.purpose: Default for control color/background transitions (keys, toggles, rows).

motion.name: fill
motion.purpose: Limit-bar and progress fills — calm ballistics, not twitchy.

motion.name: reveal
motion.purpose: The system's one expressive easing, used for a single reveal.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Every animation, pulse, and skeleton shimmer is gated behind this query; fills snap to value under reduce.

breakpoints.name: widget-min
breakpoints.purpose: The main window's minimum width. Every band must read here without clipping — the footer wraps its Manage affordance below this pressure.

breakpoints.name: widget
breakpoints.purpose: The main window's default and design width, and the density reference for the whole system. The window is freely resizable on both axes, so the density never scales with it: a wider widget gives its bands more room at the same gutter and type ladder.

components.name: Limit Cell
components.description: The signature component: rounded percent, 8px window label, and a 4px severity track on the flat plane. No box, no border — the cell is a region of the surface.

components.name: Toggle Strip
components.description: Range and breakdown-mode selection. Transparent at rest; the pressed state is an 8% white fill plus brightness — never a hue, which would compete with severity.

components.name: View Switcher

components.name: Sync Pill
components.description: Freshness as text and a hairline dot — no capsule. A polite live region; its degraded variants stay slate because a freshness pill never turns red.

components.name: Update Invitation
components.description: The app's only update affordance, centered in the titlebar and rendered only when a release was found. Brand cyan because it is an invitation, not an alarm.

components.name: Band Rule
components.description: The only structural device in the system. One hairline between two bands — never a border on each, never a card around either.

narrative.overview: Quill is an instrument, not a dashboard. The whole app is one flat plane — a single near-black surface (#14181f) ruled into bands by hairlines, carrying nothing that is not a number, a label, or the shape of a number. No cards, no raised panels, no gradients, no glow. Depth is spent only on layers that genuinely leave the plane: a dropdown, a tooltip, a dialog. This is the discipline of a glass cockpit taken to its conclusion: keep the severity meter, the tabular figures, and the strict color budget, and remove the last of the chrome — the boxes. The system runs at one density, set at the always-on-top widget's 360px design width: a 14px gutter, an 8/10/12/16px vertical ladder, 10px base type. The window is freely resizable on both axes and the density does not scale with it, so every band must stay fluid from a 320px minimum up to a full-screen drag. The legacy Manage, settings, and release-notes windows keep their current roomier density until their own redesign pass; that is a stated migration exception, not a second doctrine.
keyCharacteristics: One flat surface for the whole widget; bands are separated by hairlines, never by boxes.
A reserved three-color severity meter (green / amber / red) is the system's spine and carries no other meaning.
Color is identity or severity, never decoration; chrome is grayscale and degraded reads are slate.
Numbers are tabular and never reflow; values are bright, labels are dim.
Type runs 8px to 26px, with 8px as a hard floor.
A single density; motion is short, functional, and reduced-motion aware.

rules.name: The Severity Code Rule
rules.body: Green, amber, and red are reserved for threshold state. They never decorate, brand, or indicate category, and they never mark a failed or degraded read — that is slate. A delta takes green or red only when its meaning is known to be good or bad; unknown goodness stays neutral.

rules.name: The Reserved-Status Rule
rules.body: Provider identity and metric identity never overlap the severity meter in either direction. Where a diverging pair is a category rather than a threshold (added versus removed lines), it is drawn from the metric ramp, never from green/red.

rules.name: The Cyan Dual-Role Rule
rules.body: Signal Cyan #22d3ee is Quill's brand accent and the runtime/throughput metric hue. Both roles are Quill speaking about itself, which is why cyan is never assigned to a provider family. Cyan is not an interactive accent: selection and focus remain Signal Blue.

rules.name: The Model-Shade Rule
rules.body: A model is a shade of its provider's family ramp, assigned by in-scope rank; rank seven and beyond folds to neutral. Identity always renders swatch plus raw id, and the same model keeps the same shade on every surface of a view.

rules.name: The Dimming Ladder Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is built by brightness, not hue. Step down Text Hi to Text to Label to Faint. Reach for a new color only when it carries new meaning.

rules.name: The No-Decorative-Gradient Rule
rules.body: Gradients are permitted in exactly one place: the vertical fade under a chart area, where it is the series' own value-encoding surface. No gradient backgrounds, buttons, borders, headers, or text.

rules.name: The 8px Floor Rule
rules.body: No text renders below 8px. 8px is reserved for non-essential orientation labels (window names, axis ticks); anything a user must read to act is 10px or larger.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every live or comparative number uses tabular figures. A readout that reflows as its value ticks is broken.

rules.name: The Mono-for-Truth Rule
rules.body: Monospace is for things that are code or identifiers. It is never used on a label to look technical; jitter-free digits are tabular-nums, not a mono font.

rules.name: The Floats-Only Rule
rules.body: A shadow means 'this floats'. A region of the plane never has one. Glow, neon, and colored shadows are forbidden.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure is carried by 1px lines at 4-6% white and by the spacing ladder. Two adjacent bands get one rule between them, never a rule each.

dos: Do build on one flat surface and separate bands with a hairline and space.
Do reserve green / amber / red for threshold state on the 50% / 80% thresholds, and render degraded or failed reads in slate.
Do give every provider exactly one fixed family hue (Claude orange, Codex blue, MiniMax violet, Agent orchid) and shade models within their provider family by in-scope rank.
Do keep metric hues on sparkline strokes, endpoints, and swatches only — values stay Text Hi.
Do set font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on every live or compared number, and keep type at 8px or above.
Do make values bright and labels dim; build hierarchy with brightness and weight, not new hues.
Do keep motion functional and fast and honor prefers-reduced-motion.
Do expose the value: progressbar roles, live regions, and labeled button groups, so nothing is inferred from pixel width.
donts: Don't introduce a card, a panel border, or a second resting surface; a band that needs separating needs a rule and more space.
Don't use a gradient anywhere except a chart area's own surface fade, and never a shadow on anything that has not left the plane.
Don't ship a generic SaaS template: no gradient hero, no big-number metric panels, no pill buttons, no identical card grids.
Don't reach for AI-hype / crypto finishes: no glassmorphism, no glow, no colored shadows.
Don't go playful-consumer: no bubbly palette, no radius above 12px (the shell) or 8px (anything inside it), no emoji, no mascots.
Don't let a provider or metric hue borrow a status color, or let a status color mark a failed read.
Don't color a selected state; selection is an 8% white fill plus brightness, and focus is signal-blue.
Don't render text below 8px, or use proportional figures for live numbers.
Don't put editable controls in the widget; search, forms, and settings belong in the management windows.
